productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The art is amazing. Great bold lines and very evocative. There's one image per page, so no worries about ink/markers showing on the other side of a page. The paper has a light warm tone to it. That helps the final art look more vintage, but might be a plus or minus depending on the effect you're going for (and not clashing with cool colors).The paper is a surprisingly decent medium weight. It is smooth and takes alcohol markers well. The paper quality and one image per page makes this coloring book great for alcohol markers.The book spine lies flat easily, so that's a plus for easy coloring. The major arcana and all the court/face cards are full-paged, while the non-court cards are combined 3 to a page. Knaves and Knights of each suit are combined in one image on one page. And Kings and Queens of each suit are combined in one image on one page.The only con is that the pages aren't perforated, so not easy to remove page for framing. And this artwork is so frameable.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I like that this book has ample space to color and I like the style of the illustrations. If you are looking for more “tattoo” like art, the cover can be deceptive. I saw a few reviews disagreeing with the Christianity undertones, but if you study the Rider-Waite-Smith deck, the illustrations smith drew and Waite wanted had a lot of religious symbolism. For instance, the Hebrew letter Yod coming off the tower card. Also if you tie it into Kabbalah, you can’t help but draw on religious/spiritual symbolism. Regardless of whether Church agrees with the tarot or not, the symbols are often universal with meaning recognized across the world. Although not strictly true to the artwork of Rider-Waite, you can certainly explore the aspects of the archetypes with this coloring book. Also, I saw some reviews that said the Empress was missing, but she is present in my copy.Happy Coloring!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Slightly disappointed. The artwork on the cover of this book is a bit misleading as to what's actually inside. It has some pretty heavy religious undertones which is sort of odd, considering it's literally a TAROT coloring book. I was expecting it to be more of a traditional or "old school" tattoo type of imagery based on the cover (all that was shown in the ad) but in reality it's more like biblical imagery...? I'm a little confused because normally religion and tarot don't exactly mesh, at least not in my experience. If that's your thing, then cool nothing wrong with that. It's just not mine and not what I thought I was spending my money on. I wish the ad would have shown some of the pages on the inside because I probably wouldn't have bought if it did. But I'll share some so hopefully if that's also not your thing, you can save your money and take it elsewhere lol. On the other hand, it is really good quality paper. Thick and sturdy. Alcohol markers do bleed through but honestly that's to be expected. It also has a description of each card and it's meaning on the opposite page from the image which is a nice touch. Unfortunately that isn't enough to save it for me. Hopefully this review will give you a better idea of what you're actually buying and don't judge a book by its cover lol.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Better Then ExpectedWow, what a fun product! productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'll admit it - this book had me at "Badass Women." The Badass Women of Greek Mythology Coloring Book by Meel Tamphanon is a fun, beautifully illustrated coloring book of powerful woman.The book is made up of 45 line drawings of 45 women from Greek mythology. Though intended to be a coloring book, I think it functions nicely as a collection of stand-alone line drawings- I'm not sure if I'll actually color it. I kind of like it in black and white. It reminds me of the white marble classical busts that you see in museums. The artist's style is to not have pupils drawn in any of the eyes, which also gives it an air of classical busts carved from marble.The selection of women run the gamut of famous figures I've heard of to little-known heroines. The first page is a table of contents and then each page is a different woman. The paper is very thick and is printed on the front side only. The table of contents has a short blub about each woman, but some are more descriptive than others. EG Medusa is "The Gorgon." I'll be honest, I'm familiar with the myth of Medusa (aka woman with a perpetually horrible hair day), but not so much what a Gorgon is. That's the one complaint I have about this book - I really wish there were just a few more pages that gave like 3-4 sentences about what makes them a badass. Or it could be printed on the reverse of each page.Overall I love this book - it's great for anyone who likes Greek mythology, coloring books, or just badass women.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As both a fan of coloring books and Greek mythology, I was very excited for this coloring book, as were the older kids in the family. I thought it was great that all of the figures in this book are not only listed in alphabetical order, but also have a small descriptor in a list at the front of the book.I was so happy to see that not only are these coloring pages single sided, they're also perforated! This means we can take out a sheet for everyone who wants a page to work on without sacrificing a design on the other side. The perforation on this particular book has torn cleanly so far for us. The paper is thick enough that markers don't bleed completely through so as to need another sheet of paper underneath to protect from ink splotches, but the marker lines are definitely visible through the paper.The only issues we've had are that there are sometimes lines that are uneven & very pixelated, especially in the finer lines. We've also noticed several spots in the few pages we've done so far where the lines are clipping through. I've attached examples of both the jagged lines and the unusual clipping, which is especially noticeable on Medusa with the locks of her snake hair through her shoulder and collarbone, but there was also some clipping with her hair & wings, too. It's not a huge deal and won't be as noticeable if you're using darker markers which will obscure those illogical lines, but it would have been nice if they would have at least done a once over to catch these things.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Durable Paper for Bold Alcohol Markers
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This coloring book is a great find for fans of Greek mythology. The illustrations are detailed and expressive, living up to the "badass" title. At just under $10, you get a significant variety of characters, and the overall construction of the book feels high-quality.PAPER QUALITYThe paper has a noticeable texture and is thick enough to handle alcohol markers without tearing or pilling. Because the pages are one-sided, you don't have to worry about ruining a design on the back. However, you will still need to place a protective sheet behind your work to manage the expected bleed-through onto the next page.LAYOUT AND FRAMINGThere is one design drawback to consider: the page layout. While the pages are perforated for easy removal, the tear-off line overlaps with the image. If you intend to frame your finished pieces, you may lose a small portion of the artwork along that edge when you take the page out of the book.KEY TAKEAWAYS* (+) Marker Friendly: The thick paper holds up well to heavy ink saturation.* (+) One-Sided Designs: Eliminates the risk of ink bleeding onto a second illustration.* (+) Wide Variety: Includes 45 different figures from Greek lore.* (-) Framing Limitations: The perforated edge can cut into the actual artwork.* (-) Bleed-Through: A buffer sheet is necessary to protect the rest of the book.4 out of 5 stars? The paper and artwork are excellent, but the perforated edge cutting into the image is a slight design flaw.Is the price justified at $9.99?Absolutely. Most coloring books with one-sided, high-quality paper retail for closer to $15. Getting 45 detailed designs for $10 is a very good deal.FINAL THOUGHTSIf you enjoy using alcohol markers and are interested in Greek mythology, this book is a great value. The paper quality stands out for this price point. Just be aware of the edge design if you plan on displaying your finished work in a frame!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This coloring book has a really fun concept—featuring a range of goddesses, mortals, and monsters from Greek mythology—and it stands out for its creative approach to each character’s design.One of the biggest pros is that the pages are single-sided, so you can use markers without worrying about bleed-through ruining the next image. The pages are also perforated, which makes it easy to tear them out cleanly if you want to color outside of the book.I especially liked how each goddess’s page includes design elements tied to her mythos. For example, Arachne is surrounded by web and spider motifs, Artemis has her bow, and so on. It adds a layer of storytelling to the artwork. That said, it would have been nice if there were even a short one-line description for each figure. Not everyone is familiar with every character in Greek mythology, and a little context would go a long way.There are also some noticeable quirks in the artwork. The goddesses’ ears have a strange, swirled look that’s a bit hard to interpret, and there are other odd design choices—like Callisto’s bear having lips that blend into its tongue. In some illustrations, arms don’t quite connect naturally to the body, almost like they were added in as an afterthought. If you closely examine the details, the artwork doesn’t always hold up.That said, taken as a whole, it’s still a solid coloring book. The paper quality is good, the single-sided pages are marker-friendly, and the designs are imaginative and different from the usual offerings. Despite some artistic inconsistencies, it’s a good value for the price and an enjoyable pick for mythology fans or anyone looking for something a little more unique to color.

From the Publisher
Major Arcana 
The 22 Major Arcana cards represent archetypes drawn from mythology and medieval society. These cards will more often concern deeper, more life-impacting matters. Although they can be read for their individual meanings, they can also be seen as part of a larger journey. 
Each card is numbered from one to 21, with The Fool as zero (which is kind of a step up; at one time that card was not even numbered). We will talk about the cards in numerical order, listing the most common attributes associated with them and some suggestions for how you can think through their implications. 
Don’t think of these descriptions as definitions or sure things. They are more like jumping-off points—the starting point of a journey into your inner self and your possible futures. 
Minor Arcana 
The Minor Arcana look more like the modern-day playing cards that evolved from them. 
Each suit is associated with a different element, or facet of life. 
Wands: Fire, energy, creativity, spirit (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius) 
Coins: Earth, money, things (Capricorn, Taurus, Virgo) 
Cups: Water, emotions, intuition, feelings (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces) 
Swords: Air, intellect, knowledge, change (Aquarius, Gemini, Libra)

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update:  I was wrong; this book different paper than the other books.  The other paper takes small amounts of water decently.  Especially if you take the color off the tip of watercolor pencils with a damp brush.  This book didn't take that technique as well.Wow, this book is very, very cute.  It's a little larger than Mayo's other books, but still smaller than most adult coloring books.  I love small books, probably because I'm a slower colorer.  I really like most of the pictures.  I was also pleasantly surprised that this book doesn't have a lot of the Zentangle or doodle art patterns that a few of her books are very heavily decorated with.  There are some flower patterns on some of the critters, and the water is done in Lulu's trademark Zentangle-esque style, but it's not as visually busy.  There are a few exceptions, like The Fool.  There are tons of flowers in her work in this, as always.  The paper feels like the same horrible paper all her other books use.  Out of all the coloring book paper types, I hate it the most.  I'd much rather color on "Amazon paper." In fact, I sometimes wish she'd release a version of each book through Amazon's KDP print-on-demand platform.Each "card" has a very simple "meaning" with it.  I didn't realize that there's also already a Mayo kawaii tarot deck.  If I get back into reading tarot, I might pick up a copy.  Tarot reading isn't something that comes easily to me, though.  Time will tell.
